en: The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī Mantra for the Subjugation and Elimination of Poisonous Harm Spoken by Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
translated by the lay devotee Zhu Nanti (whose name means "Dharma-Joy" in the Jin language) of India during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying at Vaiśālī, in the Mahāvana Kūṭāgāra Śālā of the Āmrapālī Vana,
together with twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus.
All were arhats whose outflows were exhausted;
they would not undergo further existence, being like refined pure gold.
Their bodies and minds were serene and still, and their six supernormal powers were unimpeded.
Their names were Śāriputra of Great Wisdom,
Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Mahākāśyapa, Mahākātyāyana, Subhūti, and Aniruddha.
Kapphiṇa, Gavāmpati, Piṇḍola-Bhāradvāja, Bakkula,
Nanda, Ānanda, and Rāhula.
These and others were well-known to the multitude;
they were constantly revered by the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas.
Furthermore, there were twenty thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas present together with them.
He has fully accomplished all the fundamental practices of great wisdom;
he has subdued his faculties and fulfilled the six perfections;
he possesses the majestic deportment of a Buddha, and his mind is as vast as the ocean.
Their names were the youth Mañjuśrī, the youth Ratnacandra,
the youth Candraprabha, the youth Ratnakūṭa,
and the youth Garbha.
The Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla was together with sixteen of his peers;
Maitreya Bodhisattva and twenty thousand other such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were also present.
At that time, the World-Honored One was respectfully surrounded by the fourfold assembly, the devas, nāgas, the eight classes of supernatural beings, humans, and non-humans.
At that moment, all the people of the kingdom of Vaiśālī were afflicted by a great and malignant disease.
First, his eyes were red like blood;
second, pus flowed from both ears;
third, blood flowed from within his nose.
Fourth, the tongue becomes locked and voiceless.
Fifth, whatever food is consumed turns into coarse and astringent matter.
Sixth, consciousness is obstructed, as if one were intoxicated.
There are five yakṣas named Kiṇakāra;
their faces are black as ink and they have five eyes.
With fangs protruding upward like dogs, they suck the vital essence from humans.
At that time, in the great city of Vaiśālī,
there was an elder named Candracchattra, who,
together with five hundred elders of his own kind, [was present].
They went together to where the Buddha was, and having arrived, they prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet and withdrew to stand to one side.
They addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"The people of this country have encountered a great and terrible plague."
Even the skilled physician Jīvaka, though he has exhausted all his arts and skills, cannot save him.
We only pray that the World-Honored One, out of compassion for all beings,
will rescue us from the suffering of illness and cause us to be free from affliction.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the elder,
saying: "Not far from here, directly to the west,
there is a Buddha, a World-Honored One, named Amitāyus."
In that place there are two bodhisattvas named Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
They constantly regard all beings with great compassion, pitying them and rescuing them from suffering and distress.
You should now prostrate yourself before them with your five limbs touching the ground and pay them homage.
Incense should be burned and flowers scattered while focusing the mind on counting the breaths.
For the duration of ten recitations, without allowing the mind to wander,
one should, for the sake of all sentient beings, invoke that Buddha and the two Bodhisattvas.
When these words were spoken, within the Buddha’s light,
one beheld the Buddha Amitāyus of the West together with his two Bodhisattvas.
Through the Tathāgata’s spiritual power, the Buddha and the Bodhisattvas all arrived in this land.
They went to Vaiśālī and stood at the threshold of the city gate;
the Buddha, the two bodhisattvas, and the great assembly emitted a great radiance that illuminated all of Vaiśālī, turning it entirely golden.
At that time, the people of Vaiśālī prepared willow twigs and pure water and presented them to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
The Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara,
out of pity and for the sake of protecting all sentient beings, spoke this mantra and addressed all beings, saying:
You all should now, with single-minded devotion, recite:
"Homage to the Buddha; homage to the Dharma; homage to the Saṅgha.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara."
"O Greatly Compassionate One of Great Renown, Savior from Suffering and Calamity.
Thus one recites the names of the Triple Gem three times,
and recites the name of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara three times.
Burning various kinds of renowned incense and prostrating with the five limbs touching the ground,
they focused their minds single-pointedly toward the western direction to settle their breath,
invoking Avalokiteśvara to escape from suffering and calamity.
Joining his ten fingers and palms together, he spoke these verses:
"May you rescue me from my suffering and distress! With great compassion covering all, may you universally radiate pure light To extinguish and eliminate the darkness of ignorance."
To avoid the suffering of slaughter, afflictions,
and various diseases that would surely come upon me, you grant me great peace and happiness;
I now prostrate in homage to you, the one whose very name delivers from calamity.
I now take refuge in you, The compassionate father of the world;
I pray that you will surely come, To free me from the suffering of the three poisons,
And bestow upon me the happiness of this life As well as great nirvāṇa.
He addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, such a divine mantra is certainly auspicious;
it is the seal of the dhāraṇī of the great kindness and great compassion of all Buddhas of the ten directions throughout the past, present, and future."
Those who hear this mantra will have all their sufferings forever exhausted;
they shall always attain peace and happiness, remain far removed from the eight difficulties,
and achieve the samādhi of mindfulness of the Buddha, seeing the Buddha manifest before them.
I shall now proclaim the divine mantra for the protection of sentient beings by the Buddhas of the ten directions.

*Tadyathā*: *gaṅgo* (the *gaṅ* is pronounced with a retroflex *ṅa*, meaning "O, woe!"), *nīma-hoḍi* (meaning "ghosts with beautiful throats"), *moḍi-nīma* (meaning "ghosts of delusion"), *juva-nīma* (meaning "ghosts who terrify people"), *daṃba-nīma* (meaning "ghosts who rebel against people"), *aṇḍali* (meaning "those who are not pure").
*Gītpaṭāla* is named the White Ghost-Head; *Pāṭe* is named the Blue Ghost; *Paṃpaṭācarā* is named the Mother of Ghosts;
the preceding *Mātṛ* is *Vasitā*; *Tadyathā* is thus; *Ili-mili* is named the Ghost-Remover;
*Tiri-suri* is named the Ghost that Betrays Men; *Kāpali* is named the Ghost who Wears Skulls, and...
Bā-zhā (縛著) [binds]; Liǎngjí (兩頰) [both cheeks]; Qiēdīduānqí (佉鞮端耆), named the *Āśanika* (eater of children) *Kāṭikara*; Chándālī (旃陀梨), named the *Jūshén* (approaching person) *Caṇḍālī*;

Módèngqí (摩蹬耆), named the *Siǐzītóu* (lion-head) *Mātṛkā*; Mówángguǐ (魔王鬼) [the King of Demons]; Siǐzītóu (師子頭) [Lion-head]; Lèchàlèchà (勒叉勒叉) [protect, protect] all sentient beings; *Sarvasattvān* [all beings]; *Sarvapāyān* [all calamities];
*Pīyún* (埤云) [furthermore it says]; *Yīqièkěguǐ* (一切可鬼) [all possible demons]; *Zhèhèyún* (訶云) [it says "ha" (to drive away)].
*Īṅ* (long *ī*) *gatā tāta gati gati nigaṭi* (meaning "having already gone") *śūlubi śūlubi* (meaning "do not come, do not come") *rakṣa rakṣa* (meaning "protect, protect") *svāhā*.
[The Bodhisattva] said to the Buddha: "World-Honored One, such is this divine mantra."
This is what has been proclaimed by the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.

Those who recite and uphold this mantra will always be protected and sustained by all the Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas, and shall be freed from fear and spared the harm of weapons, staves, and poisons.
"And may they be freed from illness and affliction.
When these words were spoken, the people of Vaiśālī were restored to their original state.
At that time, the World-Honored One, out of compassion for sentient beings, protected all of them.
They again entreated Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva to preach the *dhāraṇī* mantra for subduing and eliminating poisonous harms.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva...
With great compassion permeating his heart and sustained by the Buddha’s spiritual power, he spoke this *dhāraṇī* mantra for destroying obstacles of evil karma and subduing poisonous harms:

*Namo buddhāya | Namo dharmāya | Namo saṃghāya | Namo Avalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | May you take pity on me and protect me from suffering; may you also protect all beings who fear, granting them great guardianship.*
Tadyathā: Dhāhuṇi (the great ghost), Mohuṇi (the water ghost), Yamavaṇi and Taṃbaṇi (the ghosts of human anger), Mohuṇi (this ghost emits fire from its mouth,
called the light-ghost), Aṃdhalī (called the flower ghost), Paṃdhalī (this ghost’s body is white, called the white ghost), Śubhi...
The name of the Emperor is *Pāṇḍaraka-bhūtanī-hūhū-lūlū*. The three-headed ghost is *Āndālī-dū-dū-lūlū*, known as the Three-Headed Child Ghost.

*Bhāṇḍālī* is the name of the Mother Black Child White Ghost. *Cū-cū-lūlū* enters into the mountains; *Cū-cū-lūlū* is known as the Good Thief. The child who dwells in the mountains is the ghost *Nirbhāṇḍālī*, known as the White-Emerging Ghost.
*Tū-tū-pū-pū-tū-tū* is the name of the Ghost Who Wishes to Depart Immediately. *Pū-pū* is the name of the Ghost Who Does Not Return Again. *Bhaṇ*.

*Caravāsiṇi* (the name of a hundred million ghosts), *Niṇḍe* (the name of more than a hundred million ghosts), *Niṇḍe* (the name of the most remembered ghosts), *Sarvāpāyakṛtā sarvanirvāṇagatā moṣaya mānuṣyān apāyān mā kuru pretān pidhāna svāhā*. Do not come!
Go away! All terrors, all poisonous harms, and all evil ghosts—upon hearing this mantra, the mouths of tigers, wolves, and lions shall immediately close.
Obstacles shall be unable to cause harm.
Those who have violated the practice of the Brahma-faring and committed the ten unwholesome karmas,
upon hearing this dhāraṇī, will be cleansed of their filth and impurities and restored to purity.
Should one have karmic obstructions, turbid evil, or unwholesome states,
by invoking Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and reciting and upholding this mantra,
one will immediately shatter those karmic obstructions and manifestly behold the Buddha.
The Buddha told Ānanda: "If there are members of the fourfold assembly who uphold the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and recite the *dhāraṇī* for eliminating and subduing poisonous harms."
One who practices this mantra will always be free from physical afflictions and mental illness.
Even if a great fire should arise from the four directions to burn their body,
by reciting and upholding this mantra, the Dragon King will send down rain, and they shall immediately attain liberation.
Even if one's body is set ablaze and every joint is in agony,
by single-mindedly reciting the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and chanting this mantra three times,
one shall immediately attain healing and recovery.
Furthermore, should they encounter famine, royal peril, wild beasts,
or bandits that cause them to lose their way;
or should they be imprisoned, confined, bound with cangues and shackles, and subjected to the fivefold fetters.
Entering the great ocean with its black winds and swirling waves,
facing the perils of water-colored mountains, yakṣas, and rākṣasas,
or being confronted by poisons, swords, and the imminent threat of execution.
Due to the karmic conditions of past deeds, one currently commits various evils;
by these causes and conditions, one undergoes all manner of suffering and extreme terror.
One should single-mindedly invoke the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Furthermore, by reciting this mantra one to seven times, poisonous harms, evil karma, evil conduct,
and the accumulation of unwholesome evils will be subdued and eliminated;
they will be utterly consumed without remainder, like fire burning wood.
For these reasons, this divine mantra spoken by the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara is called "the wondrous medicine of ambrosia bestowed upon all sentient beings. By it,
one attains freedom from the fear of illness, the fear of untimely death, and the fear of being bound.
Because they fear the three poisons of greed, anger,
and delusion, all in this Sahā world call the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara the Bestower of Fearlessness.
This dhāraṇī, the consecration formula, is the unsurpassed brahmacarya;
it is the ocean of great merit, certain in its auspiciousness.
Any sentient being who hears it shall obtain great peace and happiness, and should therefore recite it in secret.
If one wishes to recite it, one should observe the fast:
abstaining from alcohol and meat,
smearing the body with ashes, and bathing until pure.
One shall not eat asafoetida or the five pungent herbs;
one shall not consume anything that has a strong, pervasive odor.
One shall never approach women or those who are defiled.
Constantly mindful of the Buddhas of the ten directions and the Seven World-Honored Buddhas,
single-mindedly invoke Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and recite this mantra;
you shall behold Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva in person in this very life.
All their virtuous aspirations shall be fulfilled.
In future lives, they shall be born before the Buddhas and be forever parted from suffering.
The Buddha told Ānanda: "In the great city of Rājagṛha, there was a woman."
She was possessed by an evil spirit named Caṇḍālī.
That spirit came in the form of a man day and night to harass her;
its essence entered her body, and she gave birth to five hundred ghost-children.
"Do you remember this matter?
At that time, I instructed this woman to invoke the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva."
With a continuous stream of wholesome minds, they enter wholesome realms.
Ānanda, you should know that by the power of such bodhisattvas’ majestic spiritual authority, malevolent spirits are subdued and vanquished,
and they are able to behold my body with its incomparable form and appearance.
At that time, from each and every pore of my body, precious lotus flowers appeared;
and countless emanation Buddhas, with one voice and in unison,
praised the Great Compassionate One who bestows fearlessness.
Cause the girl to receive, uphold, read, and recite this mantra until she has mastered it.
Through the merit of this mantra, the three obstructions will be forever exhausted;
she shall escape the fires of the prison of the triple world and no longer undergo manifold sufferings.
The four hundred and four diseases shall not arise at once.
Should there be sentient beings entering an army for battle and facing imminent harm,
if they recite and remember this dhāraṇī and invoke the name of the Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika Avalokiteśvara, [they shall be saved].
Like a hawk or a falcon taking flight, one immediately attains liberation.
If there are sentient beings suffering great distress,
confined in prisons with shackles, manacles, and neck-fetters;
Furthermore, for periods of punishment lasting from one day up to ten days,
or from one month up to five months,
one should purify the mind and fix the attention on a single object.
They shall invoke Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and take refuge in the Triple Gem.
Reciting my name three times, they shall chant the six-syllable mantra of Great Auspiciousness, the Divine Incantation for Saving from Suffering,
which is spoken as follows:

Tadyathā: Antali, Pañcāli, Kijūli (the ghost named *Mālādharī*, the Garland-Bearer), Dantāli (the ghost named *Lohamuṣaladhara*, the Iron-Mace-Holder), Śaṇḍāli (the ghost named *Vāsīdhara*, the Axe-Holder), Tiya-pada (the ghost named *Puruṣaprabha*, the Light-Giver to Men), Yaśa-pada (the ghost named *Śravaṇa*, the Listener), Phala-ni-ki (the ghost named *Dīrghadanta*, the Long-Tusked One), Nanda-li (the ghost named *Mahākāya*, the Large-Body One), Bhaga-li (the ghost named *Mahāmukha*, the Large-Faced One), Aruṇe (the ghost named *Nimīlita*, the Closed-Eyed One), Bakūli (the ghost named *Ghaṇṭādharī*, the Bell-Bearer), Makūle (the ghost named *Vikīrṇakeśī*, the Disheveled-Haired One), and Dūpule (the ghost named *Guhanivāsī*, the Cave-Dweller). At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this divine mantra, [remained silent].
He addressed Ānanda, saying:
"If sons or daughters of good family among the fourfold assembly of disciples should hear the name of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara..."
Furthermore, one should receive, uphold, recite, and chant these six-character phrases.
If, while traveling through a wilderness, one becomes lost on the path,
by chanting this mantra, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva [will appear].
With great compassion perfuming their hearts,
they manifest as human beings to show them the way and lead them to safety;
if they are hungry or thirsty, they manifest as springs and wells.
Fruits, gourds, food, and drink shall cause them to be fully satiated.
Furthermore, suppose there is a person who encounters great calamity,
losing their kingdom, wife, children, and property, and meeting with those they loathe.
Invoke the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and recite this mantra while counting the breaths and maintaining focused mindfulness.
Without allowing the mind to be distracted, continue this for seven times seven days.
At that time, the Great Compassionate One manifested as the form of a deva and as the form of a powerful kumbhāṇḍa rāja,
escorting them back to their own land so that they might attain peace and security.
Furthermore, if there is a person who enters the sea to gather treasures, or encounters tigers, wolves, lions, venomous insects, vipers, and scorpions in empty mountains and vast wildernesses,
or meets yakṣas, rākṣasas, and kumbhāṇḍas;
As for those evil spirits who consume vital essence,
by reciting the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva three times and chanting this dhāraṇī,
one shall immediately attain liberation.
If there is a woman who experiences difficult labor and is on the verge of death,
by three times invoking the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and reciting and upholding this mantra, she shall immediately attain liberation.
When encountering great, wicked bandits who plundered his wealth,
he invoked the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva three times and recited this dhāraṇī;
the bandits immediately felt compassion in their hearts and returned by the way they had come.
Ānanda, you should know that such a bodhisattva and this divine mantra are definitively auspicious;
they can always eliminate and subdue all poisons and harms, being truly and not falsely so.
They universally bestow fearlessness upon all sentient beings of the three realms,
providing great protection so that they may enjoy happiness in this life and,
in future births, behold the Buddhas, hear the Dharma, and swiftly attain liberation.
The majestic power and spiritual efficacy of this mantra are immeasurably sublime;
it can cause sentient beings to escape the sufferings of the hells,
the sufferings of hungry ghosts, and the sufferings of animals.
The suffering of the asuras and the suffering of the eight difficult conditions shall be extinguished forever without remainder, like water putting out fire.
Ānanda, you should know this.
If there are those who uphold the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and maintain this mantra,
they shall obtain great and virtuous benefits, subduing and eliminating all poisonous harms.
In both this life and future lives, all inauspicious matters shall be forever exhausted without remainder.
They will be fully endowed with morality, diligence, mindfulness, concentration, and dhāraṇī.
Ānanda, you should know that if anyone hears these six-word phrases, this unsurpassed divine mantra of the Physician King who saves from suffering, [they shall attain such qualities].
By reciting the name of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One, one’s defilements and impurities are eliminated;
immediately in this very body, one shall behold eight billion Buddhas all coming to extend their hands in greeting.
For their sake, he preached the merits, spiritual powers, and the six-syllable mantra of the Great Compassionate One who bestows fearlessness;
because they beheld the Buddha, they immediately attained the *anushamshin* (unforgetting) *dhāraṇī*.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"Greatly compassionate and of great renown, The auspicious one who brings peace and happiness,
He constantly utters auspicious words To rescue those in extreme suffering."
If sentient beings hear his name, they leave suffering behind and attain liberation;
he even sports within the hells, taking upon himself their suffering out of great compassion,
or dwells among the animals, manifesting in the form of an animal.
Teaching them with great wisdom, they cause them to resolve upon the Unsurpassed Mind;
whether dwelling among the asuras, they tame their minds with gentle words,
causing them to eliminate the habit of arrogance and swiftly reach the shore of the unconditioned.
Manifesting in the form of a hungry ghost, From his hands he pours forth fragrant,
colored milk for those tormented by hunger and thirst; Bestowing it so they may attain full satisfaction,
With a heart of great kindness and great compassion, He sports within the five realms of existence.
Constantly gathering wisdom through skillful means, you universally instruct all beings with the supreme and most excellent expedients,
causing them to leave behind the suffering of birth and death and always attain a state of peace and bliss, reaching the shore of Great Nirvāṇa.
At that time, having spoken these words, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"These six-syllable phrases are definitively auspicious, true, and not false."
"Whoever hears this shall obtain great and wholesome benefit and acquire immeasurable merit.
Having spoken these words,
there was a bhikṣu named Upasena in the great city of Rājagṛha.
With fierce diligence and valor, he practiced difficult and painful austerities as if his head were on fire,
staying in the forest of cremation grounds surrounded by an immeasurable multitude.
He himself recounted how, in the past, he had committed various evil deeds and killed immeasurable beings.

Upon hearing the six-syllable mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, he contemplated it with right mindfulness; by focusing his mind on the heart-channel and concentrating his visualization on a single point, he beheld Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and immediately attained liberation, becoming an Arhat.
How should one come to see Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and the Buddhas of the ten directions?
If you wish to see them,
straighten your body and rectify your mind so that the mind does not waver, maintaining a continuous flow of mental energy.
Place the left hand upon the right hand;
extend the tongue toward the palate and regulate the breath so that it is even,
ensuring the air is neither coarse nor subtle, but tranquil.
Slowly counting from one to ten, one achieves mindfulness of breathing (*ānāpānasmṛti*).
Without a distracted mind, one prevents the breath from becoming coarse;
it should neither turn outward, nor be constricted, nor be slippery.
Like an infant drinking milk, one inhales and sucks it in;
neither blue nor white, it is harmonized in the middle.
From the tip of the heart, it descends through forty channels to take hold of the single central channel.
He causes the breath to proceed peacefully from within into the fourteen channels;
from the great channel it arises and reaches beneath the tongue,
and further emerging from the tongue-channel, it reaches the tip of the tongue.
It is neither blue, nor white, nor yellow, nor black.
Like a vessel of lapis lazuli, exactly eight inches in length,
it reaches the tip of the nose and returns to the root of the heart, causing the mind to become clear and pure.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
"This six-syllable chapter of the Greatly Valiant Jewel Banner possesses the merit of great compassion that subdues and eliminates all poisonous harms."
Through this counting of breaths,
by the power of mental concentration, it is like a swift-flowing stream;
one will quickly behold Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and the Buddhas of the ten directions.
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus: "Listen well, all of you.
If you bhikṣus have already gone forth from the household life and wish to partake of the unsurpassed flavor of the Dharma, which is like ambrosia..."
One should restrain the body and not violate dignified deportment;
sitting upright in meditative absorption with a mind directed inward,
one contemplates suffering, emptiness, impermanence, decay, and the fact that all things will soon be worn away and perish.
When practicing the fivefold meditation, one should observe the body for oneself.
From the head to the feet, between each and every joint,
one must cause the mindfulness to remain fixed and not be scattered.
"Observe closely that the various joints are like a plantain tree, empty both inside and out.
You should know that form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are likewise so.
When the Buddha spoke these words,
The Venerable Śāriputra was sitting beneath a tree in the Śītavana forest;
having understood the Buddha’s intention, he sat upright in meditative absorption.
Entering into samādhi, his body became the color of pure gold,
causing countless people who saw him to rejoice and resolve to attain bodhicitta.
At that time, Upasena rose from his seat.
He approached the Venerable Śāriputra,
prostrated with his head at the ground to touch the Master’s feet in salutation,
and said to him: "Venerable One," he addressed him.
Just now, the Tathāgata praised the practice of counting the breaths.
By this cause and condition, one obtains great and wholesome benefit.
How does one count the breaths? We only pray that the Venerable One will explain this for us.
How do the eye and eye-consciousness, in their association with forms, maintain their grasp?
How do the ear and ear-consciousness, in their association with sounds, maintain their grasp?
How do the nose and nose-consciousness, in their association with odors, maintain their grasp?
How is the tongue and tongue-consciousness, which correspond with flavors, maintained?
How is the mind and mental consciousness, which correspond with objects of perception, maintained?
How are the various inverted perceptions, which correspond with inversions, maintained?
How are form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and fine textures to be restrained?
And how is this thief of consciousness, which runs like a monkey and frolics among the six sense faculties while universally objectifying all phenomena, to be restrained?
Then Śāriputra said to Upasena:
"You should now observe that the earth element has no nature of solidity,
and the water element does not abide as a substance."
The wind element and the nature of wind are unimpeded.
From inversion arises fire, and the nature of fire is unreal.
Form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness arise dependently upon causes and conditions.
Each and every nature and characteristic is identical to those of water, fire, wind, and so forth;
they all enter the limit of reality as it is.
When Upasena heard these words, he...
With his body like water or fire, he attained the meditative concentration of the four great elements;
he thoroughly penetrated that the five aggregates are empty and non-existent;
having slain the bandits of the fetters, his mind was suddenly and completely liberated.
Having attained the state of an Arhat, he emitted fire from his body and immediately shattered his own form to enter parinirvāṇa.
At that time, Śāriputra collected his relics.
Having erected a stupa above it,
he paid homage to the Buddha and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
the Buddha has taught that meditative concentration is the foremost nectar and the unsurpassed flavor of the Dharma."
If there are those who practice this, their bodies will become like lapis lazuli, and they will see the Buddhas within every pore.
They will contemplate ignorance, volitional formations, and so forth, up to old age and death,
seeing that the essential nature and characteristics of each are entirely unreal.
It is like an echo in an empty valley; it is like a plantain tree, lacking any core substance.
It is like a mirage in the heat; it is like the movement of wild horses.
It is like a city of the Gandharvas; it is like a bubble upon the water.
Like an illusion, like a transformation, like dew, and like lightning—
contemplating each link of the twelvefold chain of dependent origination in this way, they realize the path of a pratyekabuddha;
or they enter the tranquil concentration of the lapis lazuli samādhi.
Seeing the Buddhas in countless numbers, they gave rise to the unsurpassed mind.
They cultivated the conduct of a youth and dwelt in non-retrogression. The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"Just as Upasena heard me speak these verses on great compassion and the method of the concentration on counting the breath."
He destroyed countless billions of blazing evils;
he attained arhatship, endowed with the precepts, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation.
Water and fire issued from his body, and he entered parinirvāṇa by the dissolution of his physical form.
They cause countless people to give rise to great wholesome minds.
Śāriputra, you should know that if good men or good women hear the name of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara’s great compassion, [they shall attain liberation].
Furthermore, by means of the six-syllable mantra that subdues and eliminates poison and harm,
and the method of counting the breath while maintaining mindfulness of pure conduct,
one eradicates the evil karma created over incalculable eons and destroys the obstructions of evil karma.
In this very life, they shall behold immeasurable and boundless Buddhas;
they shall hear the preaching of the sublime Dharma without hindrance according to their wishes;
and they shall give rise to the three kinds of pure bodhicitta.
If there are karmic conditions from past lives or extremely grave evil deeds committed in the present,
one may see Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva in a dream.
Just as a great, violent wind blows through heavy clouds, scattering them in all directions,
so too shall they be freed from their heavy sins and evil karma to be born before the Buddhas.
Having spoken these words, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra:
I now, for this purpose, uphold the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
I shall recite these unsurpassed verses and phrases that subdue and eliminate poison and harm,
and offer praise through verse.

I command Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the others to protect with a compassionate heart those who uphold this sutra and hear the name of the Great Compassionate One; just as the Dharma-ministers of the Heavenly Son protect me,
I command the sea dragon Elāpattra to protect with a compassionate heart those who uphold this sutra.
Just as one protects one’s eyes or loves one’s own child, never departing from me day or night during the six periods;
I command the yakṣas and rākṣasas, and countless male and female nāgas,
to protect with a compassionate heart those who uphold this sutra, so that they may not dare to touch them, just as one would not dare to touch the crown of one’s head.
I command King Virūḍhaka to protect with a compassionate heart those who uphold this sutra,
never wearying— just as a mother loves her child— guarding them day and night whether they are walking or staying still.
I command Nanda, Upananda, Sāgara, and Upendra.
With a heart of loving-kindness, they protect those who uphold this sutra, honoring, making offerings to, and prostrating at their feet—
just as the devas revere Śakra, as a filial son respects his parents,
as a poor man guards his treasure, and as the blind require eyes and a true guide.
I command all spirits and ghosts, small dragons, venomous snakes, and predatory beasts,
as well as all wicked people and those of foul speech: if you oppose this mantra and give rise to unwholesome thoughts,
you shall manifest leprosy, pus, and blood in this life, and thereafter fall into hell for long nights of suffering.
Therefore, one should protect it with a compassionate heart; by upholding, receiving, reading, and reciting these words of empowerment, one’s hellish rebirths will be purified like a lotus.

Hungry ghosts shall be shattered, the eight difficulties shall cease, and in a future life, one shall be born before a Buddha and enter samādhi. One will certainly attain the stage of non-retrogression.
Universally bestowing great peace and happiness upon all, I teach all sentient beings to cultivate the ten stages (*bhūmi*).
From countless Buddhas of the past, I heard this mantra for subduing and eliminating poison and harm;
It eliminates the three obstructions and removes all evils, Fulfilling the five eyes and bringing one to the realization of *bodhi*.
Forever acting as parents to the three realms, Bestowing peace and happiness so that all may find rest;
Should there be those who hear my name, And likewise hear the name of the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara,
Who recite and uphold this dhāraṇī, they shall be free from all evils, And shall not fall into the realms of hell or the animal kingdom.

Born by transformation from a lotus as the parents, With a mind pure, supple, and free from defilement, One will surely hear the unsurpassed, great, and luminous wisdom; With a mind as stable as the earth, it cannot be moved.
Whenever all Buddhas appear in the world, Their illumination shines like the sun and the moon.
From his body issues forth the light of great wisdom, like the blazing of a mountain of purple gold;
from among the thirty-two marks flow forth the eighty secondary signs,
resembling Mount Sumeru reflected and made manifest within the great ocean.
Sentient beings who hear his name shall forever leave the three evil realms and dwell in the state of the unconditioned;
they shall always delight in great nirvana.
All Buddhas appear in the world for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to sentient beings.
With diverse mouths and each their own body, Sitting upright upon the vajra-throne,
Mouths emit five-colored light; With tongues shaped like lotus petals,
they praise the Great Compassionate One, The Tamer who teaches the Lion Dharma.
"World-Protector Avalokiteśvara, you who are certain to eliminate all harms and purify the roots of the three poisons,
you will undoubtedly attain the path of Buddhahood.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this verse, [remained silent].
In order to protect this sutra for those who uphold the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
he spoke the Auspicious Consecration Dhāraṇī and uttered the mantra as follows:

Tadyathā: Udambili (the mountain-dwelling ghost), Dum-bili (the cave-dwelling ghost), Danda (the "rotting-eye" ghost), Paradanda (the "eater of leftover fruit" ghost who dwells beneath all fruit trees), Natta-Sunatta (the "fond of stealing" ghost), Kibbisa (the "fish-killer" ghost), Monaya (the "renunciant" ghost), Samaya (the "samādhi" ghost), Dandini (the "staff-wielder" ghost), Nirakisi (the "fine-haired woman" ghost), Palagubi (the "dweller in broken skin" ghost), Uli (the "necklace" ghost), and Kukkuli (the "tail" ghost). The Buddha said to Śāriputra: "Such are the verses of this consecrated dhāraṇī, which are definitively auspicious. Should anyone hear, receive, uphold, read, or recite them..."
One shall destroy the obstructions of evil karma and never die an untimely death.
Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, such a divine mantra is a phrase of great auspiciousness."
"Universally bestowing fearlessness upon all beings—
World-Honored One, from which Buddha did you hear these words in the past?
We only pray that the World-Honored One will analyze and explain them for us."
May all beings in future ages universally hear and know this,
so that they may attain great peace and happiness, be spared from untimely death,
and remain unharmed by swords, staves, poisons, water, fire, or thieves.
The Buddha told Śāriputra: "Since I was in the presence of immeasurable Buddhas of the past, I have heard these phrases, received and upheld them, and recited them;
immediately, I attained transcendence from the offenses of birth and death for eighty million kalpas."
Furthermore, he recalled that eighty thousand kalpas ago there was a Buddha,
a World-Honored One named Sarvalokābhibhū,
who was fully endowed with the ten titles.
That Buddha, the World-Honored One, expounded the aforementioned verses for me.
I immediately practiced counting the breaths so that my mind would not be distracted;
suddenly, the sounds dissolved and my fetters and afflictions were subdued.
They shall attain the stage of non-arising dharma-patience and dwell in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
If good men or good women hear this sutra, receive and uphold it,
read and recite it, copy it, and explain it;
One immediately attains transcendence from the sins of birth and death throughout immeasurable, incalculable, and asankhyeya kalpas;
one subdues poisonous harms and is not confronted by calamities.
When the Buddha spoke these words,
Five hundred sons of elders attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Innumerable humans and devas resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Śāriputra, Ānanda, and the others addressed the Buddha, saying:
World-Honored One, this Ocean of Samādhis for Contemplating the Buddha,
and the Dhāraṇī Mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva for Eliminating and Subduing Poisonous Harm,
bring all auspiciousness to every place they reach.
"Just as the Brahmā King is beloved and revered by the multitude, so it is, Ānanda;
it is exactly as you have said. If a son of good family or a daughter of good family should hear even the title of this sutra."
They shall always behold the Buddhas and the various bodhisattvas;
endowed with roots of goodness, they will be born in pure Buddha-lands.
When this chapter was being taught, [the earth shook in six ways].
Eight billion devaputras, devakanyās, nāgas, ghosts,
and spirits all rejoiced and resolved upon the bodhicitta;
so too did Śāriputra, Ānanda, and the others.
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they paid homage to the Buddha and withdrew.
[End of] the *Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī Mantra for the Elimination and Subjugation of Poisonous Harm Spoken by Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*.
